Or let the world know your project is using Cypress with the badge below. ``` ```
readmeHtml:
Documentation | Changelog | Roadmap

The web has evolved. Finally, testing has too.

Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

Join us, we're hiring.


What is Cypress?

Installing

Install Cypress for Mac, Linux, or Windows, then get started.

npm install cypress --save-dev

or

yarn add cypress --dev

or

pnpm add cypress --save-dev

Contributing

- develop branch

Please see our Contributing Guideline which explains repo organization, linting, testing, and other steps.

License

This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT license.

Badges

Configure a badge for your project's README to show your test status or test count in the Cypress Cloud.

Or let the world know your project is using Cypress with the badge below.

[![Cypress.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20with-Cypress-04C38E.svg)](https://www.cypress.io/)

aiSummary.oneLiner: A fast, reliable, and developer-friendly end-to-end testing framework for modern web applications
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Cypress is a next-generation front-end testing tool built for the modern web. Unlike older frameworks that rely on external WebDriver protocols, Cypress executes directly within the same run-loop as the application being tested, providing synchronous access to the DOM and eliminating the flakiness commonly associated with asynchronous testing. It supports both comprehensive end-to-end (E2E) testing and isolated component testing for popular frameworks like React, Angular, Vue, and Svelte. The tool offers an interactive test runner that allows developers to time-travel through test states, debug visually in real-time, and ensure high application reliability.
keyFeatures: In-browser execution: runs tests within the same environment as the application, ensuring faster execution and direct DOM access.
Time-travel debugging: takes snapshots as tests run, allowing developers to hover over commands in the Command Log to see exactly what happened at each step.
Automatic waiting: automatically waits for commands and assertions before moving on, eliminating the need for arbitrary sleep or wait timeouts.
Network traffic control: provides the ability to stub, intercept, and mock network requests to test edge cases without backend dependencies.
Component testing: supports mounting and testing individual UI components in isolation across major JavaScript frameworks.
Cypress Cloud integration: optionally connects to Cypress Cloud to provide test parallelization, load balancing, and advanced analytics.

useCases.title: End-to-End User Journeys
useCases.description: Allows QA engineers to write reliable tests simulating complete user workflows, from logging in to completing complex transactions.

useCases.title: Component-Driven Development
useCases.description: Enables frontend developers to test isolated React or Vue components directly in the browser to ensure they render and behave correctly.

useCases.title: CI/CD Pipeline Integration
useCases.description: Integrates into automated deployment pipelines to block releases if critical application features break or regress.

useCases.title: Visual Debugging
useCases.description: Helps developers quickly identify the root cause of test failures by visually stepping through the state of the application at the exact moment of failure.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Cypress is built for frontend developers, QA engineers, and full-stack teams who need to write reliable, fast tests for modern web applications. It is widely adopted across the industry as a standard tool for both E2E and component testing.
